scope: Five named boxed/specialty product-family records supported by original Wizards articles and one official Wizards Japan product-code page. This is bounded product evidence, not a certification of individual printing or legality.

records.source_section: Global Series: Jiang Yanggu and Mu Yanling — two 60-card preconstructed decks, printed official set code GS1
records.relationship_note: Two introductory Planeswalker decks in one Global Series release; the Scryfall duel_deck type alone is not proof of a historical Duel Decks-branded matchup. Wizards' 2018 announcement limited Standard legality to China at the time; no current legality inference.

records.source_section: Secret Lair Drop Series — multiple timeboxed-to-demand artist-focused collectible drops beginning December 2, 2019
records.relationship_note: An ongoing collection of distinct drops, not one physical box despite Scryfall box typing.

records.source_section: Secret Lair: Ultimate Edition — retail display box of five enemy fetch lands beginning May 29, 2020
records.relationship_note: A five-card in-store retail collection, distinct from Secret Lair's timeboxed print-to-demand Drop Series.

records.source_section: Secret Lair 30th Anniversary Countdown Kit — collection of 30 year-themed boosters for the holiday season
records.relationship_note: Thirty year-themed card packets inside one anniversary collection; not thirty separate expansion releases.

records.source_section: Secret Lair x MSCHF: The Zeta Set — Chaos Vault release September 2, 2026, featuring playtest-style cards
records.relationship_note: The Wizards article warns of a later Pauper-rules update; this family review does not certify legalities or treat mock-playtest styling as ordinary premier-set cards.

caveats: The original Global Series 2018 Standard legality announcement was region-specific; no current legality determination is made here.
Secret Lair Drop Series SLD is an ongoing series, not one boxed item. Other Secret Lair codes denote distinct collection formats and release campaigns.
The Zeta Set Wizards article explicitly records a post-publication Pauper information update, so a set-family source is not a format-legality source.
Historical 1990s/early 2000s boxed records and Salvat/Hachette products without adequate directly reviewed Wizards evidence remain pending.
